chapter: A musical family and the old New Orleans bands
title: A Masonic funeral and the second line
summary: At about eight years old Danny saw a Masonic funeral and second-line crowd, mistaking men in aprons for waiters.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: So there's a funeral. And it's a Masonic funeral. You never seen nothin' like that. These guys got these soles and these aprons on. Because a minister died a few blocks from my house. So we say "They got second-line; let's go
and see them." I was... That's about 1917, so I was about eight years old...
When you say they got a second line, that means there's going to be a line behind the funeral.
That's the people that follow the funeral.
That follow the funeral. Second line.

They was inquisitive and they want to see. It's just a crowd. Here's something happening. They'll see who is going to perform, see how loud the widow screams, and who holds the widow. There's all kind of intrigue at a funeral. What kind of casket the late deceased, and who is there, if his woman is there, or if his wife is there, his first wife is there. There's always something.

So they'd say, "Well, let's go down there." My Uncle Lucien and Willie, the younger ones, said, "Let's go down there to the band(?) and see the funeral." So we go down there and see the funeral. I don't know what it is; all I'm seeing is guys with aprons on. So I said, "Man, they must gonna serve food. I see all these waiters.
